title: CHAPS High-Value Payment Stuck in Pending — Idempotency Key Collision

content.summary: A CHAPS high-value payment of GBP 12.5 M became stuck in PENDING state for 188 minutes on 2024-04-18 due to an idempotency key collision between two separate corporate clients whose reference numbers were hashed identically by a broken hash function introduced in a library upgrade.

timeline.event: Corporate client A submits CHAPS payment GBP 12.5 M; idempotency key generated
Corporate client B submits CHAPS payment GBP 3.1 M 200 ms later; same idempotency key generated (collision)
wire-transfer-service deduplicates client B's payment against client A's key; client B receives 200 OK but payment is not submitted
client A payment stuck in PENDING — transaction-ledger shows conflicting ownership on idempotency record
DBA team manually resolves idempotency record conflict; both payments re-submitted with corrected keys
Both CHAPS payments confirmed settled; incident resolved

content.root_cause: The idempotency key generation library was upgraded from hashlib-utils v2.1 to v3.0.0 as part of a routine dependency update. The v3.0.0 release contained a bug (upstream CVE-2024-18821) where the hash function truncated output to 32 bits instead of 256 bits for inputs shorter than 64 bytes, dramatically increasing collision probability. The library update was not subject to payment-path regression testing.
contributing_factors: Dependency upgrades not subject to payment-path integration test suite
No collision monitoring on the idempotency store (Redis)
Idempotency key namespace did not include client identifier, making cross-client collisions possible
Same root cause pattern as INC-2024-002 — shared idempotency store design weakness

immediate: Pin hashlib-utils to v2.1 across all payment services
Manually resolve idempotency key conflict in Redis
Re-submit affected payments with corrected keys
short_term: Add client identifier as namespace prefix to all idempotency keys (JIRA PAY-9200)
Add Redis idempotency collision rate monitor (JIRA PAY-9201)
Add payment-path regression tests to dependency update pipeline (JIRA PAY-9202)
long_term: Evaluate UUIDv7 as idempotency key standard across all payment services
Introduce automated CVE scanning for payment-critical library dependencies
Quarterly payment path chaos engineering exercises
